## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A single-fascicle Vinaya-ritual manual by **Dàoxuān** 道宣 ([道宣](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%81%93%E5%AE%A3), 596–667) treating the canonical regulation of monastic vestment — the *kāṣāya* (*jiāshā* 袈裟), the *saṃghāṭī*, and other ritual cloth-articles — and the institutional regulation of monastic insignia. *Zhāngfú* 章服 ("insignia and robes") refers specifically to the canonical and customary regulation of vestment; *yí* 儀 ("decorum, ceremonial rule") indicates a normative ritual manual.

**Abstract**

The *Zhāngfú yí* is the principal Tang Vinaya manual on monastic vestment regulation and the foundational document for the **Sino-Buddhist regulation of the kāṣāya**. The work synthesises canonical precedent (Indian *vinaya* prescriptions) with Chinese institutional practice and was decisive for all subsequent East Asian regulation of monastic dress. The work belongs together with [KR6k0181](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0181) *Liàngchù qīngzhòng yí* 量處輕重儀 (on monastic property), [KR6k0182](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0182) *Shìmén guījìng yí* 釋門歸敬儀 (on monastic etiquette), [KR6k0183](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0183) *Jiàojiè xīnxué bǐqiū xínghù lǜyí* 教誡新學比丘行護律儀 (on novice training), and others as part of Dàoxuān's broader institutional-ritual programme — works that translated *Sìfēnlǜ* canonical norms into operational Tang-monastic practice. Composition belongs to Dàoxuān's mature *Zhōngnán* period.
